title: Relation
description: A reified triple: `subject —predicate→ object`, authored by a person OR by a software agent (prov:SoftwareAgent) and stored on the AUTHOR's vault. When the author is a machine, the provenance of the claim belongs with it — see `model`, `confidence` and `derivedFrom`; a machine-made statement that cannot say how it was made is indistinguishable from a person's. One ontology for every lightweight edge between envelopes — a reaction (predicate 'react', value '👍'), a pin (predicate 'pin', value 'me'|'all'), a mention notification, a response to an activity (predicate 'respond') — instead of one bespoke ontology per edge kind. `object` is a w3ds envelope URI so the edge survives relocation. Distinct from the registered `Reference` ontology (c20e9437-…), which is a review/score OF a target; a Relation is a statement BETWEEN two envelopes. A cross-vault copy uses the reference mixin (isReference + canonicalOwnerEName + canonicalRelationId): the source-of-truth edge stays on the author's vault. EVERY RELATION IS AN EVENT, and the current state is a FOLD over the events in time — not the assumption that one envelope is the present. A reader that treats a single relation as current state is right only by accident: the same subject may assert, withdraw and re-assert, and three assertions at three moments are three facts. Where a platform expresses a withdrawal by DELETING the envelope, absence is the fold's result and nothing more need be read; where it expresses it with a further relation, the later one wins. `prov:atTime` is what makes the fold possible: order by when the facts HAPPENED, not by when they were written. The prefix `prov:` is http://www.w3.org/ns/prov# (PROV-O, W3C Recommendation 2013-04-30); a reified triple is exactly the "influence node" that specification says to hang qualifying detail on, so its vocabulary is used here rather than inventing names for the same ideas.

id.description: Body id (mirrors the metaEnvelope id on the canonical)

subject.description: Who/what the statement is about — an eName or a w3ds envelope URI

value.description: Predicate-specific payload: the emoji for 'react', 'me'|'all' for 'pin'

authorId.description: @-prefixed eName of whoever asserted the relation

createdAt.description: When the envelope was WRITTEN. Not when the fact happened — see `prov:atTime`.

prov:atTime.description: When the asserted fact HAPPENED, as against `createdAt`, which is when the envelope was written. The two differ whenever a relation is recorded after the event it describes — a reaction written to the vault seconds after the tap, an edge imported from elsewhere, a machine reading a recording made yesterday. A reader placing relations on a timeline MUST prefer this and fall back to `createdAt` only when it is absent. Whoever writes it should say in their platform's self-description which clock it is, because "when it happened" is only meaningful if the reader knows whose watch was used.

model.description: Machine-authored relations: which model produced the claim — the one that actually answered, not the one usually asked, since a failover names the wrong one otherwise.

promptVersion.description: Machine-authored relations: which wording produced it, so a platform can tell whether a change to its prompt improved anything.

confidence.description: Machine-authored relations: 0–1, how sure the author is. Absent means unstated, which is NOT the same as certain.

derivedFrom.description: Machine-authored relations: the envelopes or files the claim was read from, as w3ds URIs. A claim whose source cannot be named cannot be checked.

isReference.description: True on a cross-vault copy pointing at the canonical

canonicalOwnerEName.description: Reference mixin: whose vault holds the canonical

canonicalRelationId.description: Reference mixin: metaEnvelope id of the canonical

sharedBy.description: Reference mixin: who fanned the copy out
